title: Standalone Storage Spaces Component Degradation
exclusions: This use case evaluates periodic read-only PowerShell snapshots of concrete, nonprimordial Storage Spaces pools and their associated virtual and physical disks on standalone Windows systems. It reports an entity whose `HealthStatus` is not `Healthy`, whose normalized `OperationalStatus` set is not exactly `OK`, or a pool that is read-only. It does not monitor the primordial pool or unpooled/spare-disk eligibility/capacity, Storage Spaces Direct/Azure Local cluster Health Service faults, Cluster Shared Volumes, hardware RAID/SAN/vendor arrays, ordinary NTFS/ReFS/volume/file-system health, free space, latency/IOPS, SMART/vendor predictive failure, storage jobs/repair progress, enclosure/SES state, backups, data integrity, or application availability. Snapshot polling can miss a fault that begins and fully recovers between five-minute runs. `Warning`, `Unhealthy`, `Unknown`, `Degraded`, `Lost Communication`, `Detached`, `No Redundancy`, `Read-only`, and other non-OK states are observations requiring Microsoft-state guidance and local topology; they do not identify root cause. The collector performs no repair or state change.
evidence: After deployment, retain the approved standalone Storage Spaces inventory and owner; host/pool/virtual-disk/physical-disk unique IDs, names, resiliency and physical-location map; Windows/Storage module/provider versions; expected entity counts and maintenance authority; the signed/versioned collector and hash, execution identity, effective `[powershell://StorageSpacesHealth]` input, schedule, source type/index, and `btool`; complete manifest and entity rows sharing each snapshot ID; the `windows_storage_spaces_degraded_entity` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, and triggered-alert records; each result's UTC sample, entity type/ID/name, parent pool, health/operational state, read-only/detached reason, usage/location/model/firmware/resiliency context, and source metadata; same-time Storage cmdlet, Server Manager, disk/system event, storage-job, controller/enclosure/vendor, volume/application, backup, and change evidence; source/completeness/inventory results; bounded exceptions; incident disposition; and dated healthy, each-fault-branch, planned-removal, stale-source, collector-error, recovery, and end-to-end controls. This documentation-only review changed no pool/disk, ran no collector, and created no snapshot, alert, repair, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index, ingest one successful manifest and entity rows with the same `snapshot_id=spaces-positive-001`: a healthy/OK pool, a virtual disk with `health_status=Warning`, `operational_status=Degraded`, and a physical disk with `health_status=Healthy`, `operational_status=Lost Communication`. Expect exactly two result rows with reasons `health_and_operational_state` and `operational_state`. Separately set the pool to `is_read_only=true` while Healthy/OK and expect one pool row with `reason=pool_read_only`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run isolated variants and expect zero rows for a complete snapshot where every entity is `health_status=Healthy`, `operational_status=OK`, and pools are not read-only; a successful zero-pool manifest from a host not expected to have Storage Spaces; a primordial/unpooled disk not emitted by the collector; manifest and collector-error rows; an otherwise degraded entity in the newest excluded five minutes; and missing entity identity/state fields. In companion health logic, verify an expected Storage Spaces host with `pool_count=0`, incomplete entity counts, duplicate IDs, stale manifest, or `collector_error` is faulted rather than interpreted as healthy.

dataSources: A local Windows PowerShell input runs the Microsoft Storage module every 300 seconds. It queries `Get-StoragePool -IsPrimordial $false`, `Get-VirtualDisk -StoragePool <pool>`, and `Get-PhysicalDisk -StoragePool <pool>` and emits one manifest plus one row per concrete pool, virtual disk, and physical disk. The local contract is `index=windows`, `source=powershell:storage-spaces-health`, `sourcetype=windows:storage_spaces:health`; these are deployment conventions, not Microsoft/Splunk defaults. Required fields are `_time`, `host`, `schema_version`, `snapshot_id`, `sample_epoch`, `record_type`, `collector_status`, pool/virtual/physical counts, `object_type`, `object_id`, `friendly_name`, `parent_pool_id`, `health_status`, `operational_status`, `is_read_only`, reasons, resiliency/usage/location/model/firmware context, `source`, and `sourcetype`.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) version 10.0.1 for the supported Windows PowerShell input and deployment context, plus a local `windows_storage_spaces_monitor` app containing the signed collector, versioned schema, input, saved searches, and dashboard. The Microsoft Storage PowerShell module/provider is part of Windows, not a Splunk app.
spl:
index=windows source="powershell:storage-spaces-health" sourcetype="windows:storage_spaces:health" record_type="entity" earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval host=lower(trim(host)), object_type=lower(trim(object_type)), object_id=trim(object_id), friendly_name=trim(friendly_name), parent_pool_id=coalesce(trim(parent_pool_id),"none"), health_status=lower(trim(health_status)), operational_status=lower(trim(operational_status)), is_read_only=lower(coalesce(trim(is_read_only),"false"))
| where len(host)>0 AND len(object_type)>0 AND len(object_id)>0 AND len(health_status)>0 AND len(operational_status)>0 AND (health_status!="healthy" OR operational_status!="ok" OR (object_type="pool" AND is_read_only="true"))
| eval reason=case(health_status!="healthy" AND operational_status!="ok","health_and_operational_state",health_status!="healthy","health_state",operational_status!="ok","operational_state",object_type="pool" AND is_read_only="true","pool_read_only"), use_case="UC-1.2.58"
| stats latest(_time) as sample_time latest(sample_epoch) as sample_epoch latest(snapshot_id) as snapshot_id latest(friendly_name) as friendly_name latest(parent_pool_id) as parent_pool_id latest(health_status) as health_status latest(operational_status) as operational_status latest(is_read_only) as is_read_only latest(read_only_reason) as read_only_reason latest(detached_reason) as detached_reason latest(resiliency_setting) as resiliency_setting latest(usage) as usage latest(physical_location) as physical_location latest(model) as model latest(firmware_version) as firmware_version latest(reason) as reason count as observed_rows by host object_type object_id use_case
| convert ctime(sample_time)
| table sample_time host object_type object_id friendly_name parent_pool_id health_status operational_status is_read_only read_only_reason detached_reason resiliency_setting usage physical_location model firmware_version reason observed_rows snapshot_id use_case
| sort 0 host object_type friendly_name
description: Reports the latest entity row from a closed five-minute standalone Storage Spaces snapshot when a concrete pool, virtual disk, or associated physical disk is not Healthy/OK, or a pool is read-only. Each row preserves stable object/parent identity and the exact Microsoft health and operational state used for the decision.
value: A mirrored or parity space can remain online after a disk or copy fails while redundancy is reduced, and a read-only/detached pool or virtual disk can block writes or access. Component-grain snapshots shorten diagnosis, distinguish pool/virtual-disk/physical-disk impact, and let storage teams repair or replace the right layer before another failure causes data loss or outage.
implementation: Deploy the signed read-only collector only on inventoried standalone Storage Spaces hosts, emit a complete manifest and all concrete-pool/associated-entity rows every 300 seconds, and keep Storage Spaces Direct, vendor RAID/SAN, and ordinary volume monitors separate. Save the SPL as `windows_storage_spaces_degraded_entity`; run every 5 minutes over the delayed closed window; trigger per `host,object_type,object_id`; and require a later complete Healthy/OK snapshot for recovery. Validate every health/operational/read-only branch, planned removal/repair states, zero-pool/incomplete/error snapshots, stale source, duplicate deployment, safe triage, and bounded exceptions.
visualization: Build a Storage Spaces operations dashboard with expected-host manifest freshness, collector errors, count completeness, and inventory drift first; single values for unhealthy pools/virtual disks/physical disks; a host-pool-object status hierarchy; a table with state/reasons/resiliency/location/model/firmware and age; and a seven-day entity-state timeline. Drill down to every row in the same snapshot, `Get-StoragePool`/`Get-VirtualDisk`/`Get-PhysicalDisk`, storage jobs, Server Manager, disk/system events, controller/enclosure/vendor telemetry, volumes, application health, backups, and changes. Label the dashboard **standalone Storage Spaces** and link S2D/Azure Local to Health Service monitoring.
schema: Versioned local snapshot of Microsoft MSFT_StoragePool, MSFT_VirtualDisk, and MSFT_PhysicalDisk health properties
dataModelAcceleration: No CIM data model is claimed. CIM Change does not represent current Storage Spaces object health, multi-valued operational states, hierarchy, snapshot completeness, or collector state. If scale requires summary acceleration, preserve manifest counts and one row per `snapshot_id,host,object_type,object_id` with parent pool, health/operational/read-only/reason fields, schema version, and source-health markers; prove parity before alerting.

knownFalsePositives:
A result is a true non-Healthy/non-OK/read-only state under the snapshot contract. The state can be planned or transient, but should not be relabeled false without topology and recovery evidence.

1. **Planned physical-disk retirement or replacement** — `Removing From Pool`, `In Service`, `Degraded`, or related states can occur while data evacuates. Verify exact pool/disk unique ID/location, change ID, storage job/progress, redundancy, spare/capacity, operator, and UTC bounds. Preserve the state and suppress only duplicate paging during the approved operation.

2. **Approved virtual-disk detach/manual-attach or pool read-only maintenance** — Maintenance may intentionally detach a space or set policy read-only. Confirm exact object, reason (`By Policy` versus `Incomplete`), application drain, owner, change, data safeguards, and planned reattachment/read-write verification. Never suppress read-only due to quorum loss as routine policy.

3. **Firmware, HBA/controller, enclosure, cable, or power maintenance** — Devices can report Lost Communication/Transient Error during controlled work. Correlate physical location, controller/enclosure/port, firmware package/hash, power path, vendor telemetry, change, and recovery. A vendor-wide or all-maintenance exception is unsafe.

4. **Server reboot, sleep, removable enclosure, or transient reconnection** — A standalone host/enclosure can briefly enumerate non-OK. Verify boot/device timeline, subsequent complete Healthy/OK snapshot, volume/application access, and absence of repeated flaps. Suppress duplicate notification only after recovery is proven.

5. **Repair/resilver/rebalance after a real failure** — `In Service`, `Incomplete`, or degraded states can persist while repair restores copies. The alert is still correct. Correlate `Get-StorageJob`, repair progress, replacement identity, remaining redundancy, ETA, and application risk; reduce duplicate paging rather than excluding repair states permanently.

6. **Provider cache or collector/schema defect** — Incomplete discovery, null/multi-valued status rendering, or cmdlet failure can mislead. The collector must emit `collector_error`/incomplete manifest, never Healthy/OK defaults. Compare raw CIM objects, Storage module/provider version, script hash, and Server Manager.

7. **Authorized storage resilience test** — A controlled disk-removal/fault test should generate a state and later recovery. Match test ID, exact object/location, workload safeguards, expected states/timing, operator, and complete recovery. Retain as test evidence.

8. **Duplicate collectors on a host** — Two PowerShell inputs can create multiple rows/snapshots. Compare script/input deployment, snapshot IDs, host metadata, and forwarder identity; fix collection rather than suppress object health.

**Safe suppression:** preserve raw snapshots and base results. Apply notification exceptions after detection through a reviewed lookup keyed to exact host, object type/unique ID, parent pool, change/job/test ID, expected state set, owner, approver, and exclusive epoch bounds. Reject friendly-name-only, model/vendor-wide, pool-wide permanent, wildcard, or blanket maintenance exclusions; never suppress collector errors, incomplete/stale snapshots, unexpected zero pools, health worsening, lost quorum/read-only Incomplete, no redundancy, failed repair, repeated communication loss, or missing recovery.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against Microsoft Storage Spaces state guidance, Get-StoragePool/Get-VirtualDisk/Get-PhysicalDisk, standalone-disk management, and S2D Health Service scope plus Splunk Windows PowerShell input and Microsoft Windows add-on documentation; collector execution, CIM object strings, inventory, snapshots, fixtures, faults, repair/recovery, alert delivery, exceptions, and production response were specified but not executed or Microsoft/Windows storage/Splunk/hardware/application SME-signed

cost.search_load_notes: Every 5 minutes the collector emits one manifest plus one row per concrete pool and associated virtual/physical disk; typical standalone cardinality is low. Completeness and expected-inventory checks are mandatory so absent collection cannot masquerade as healthy storage.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and exact standalone scope

Assign standalone Storage Spaces, Windows, hardware, application/volume, backup, Splunk collection/content, telemetry-health, and incident owners. Inventory every expected host, concrete pool unique ID/name, virtual-disk unique ID/name/resiliency/copies, physical-disk unique ID/model/serial-safe identifier/firmware/location/controller/enclosure, volume/application mapping, expected counts, spare/capacity policy, maintenance authority, and retirement state. Friendly names are not unique enough for suppression; use provider-scoped unique IDs and parent hierarchy.

This UC replaces undocumented event-ID guesses with current-state Storage module objects. Microsoft documents every concrete pool, virtual disk, and physical disk as having high-level `HealthStatus` and one or more `OperationalStatus` values. Healthy plus exactly OK is the normal alert policy. Warning/Unhealthy/Unknown or any additional/non-OK operational state is surfaced, as is `IsReadOnly=true` for pools. Microsoft state guidance explains examples such as Degraded, Lost Communication, Detached, No Redundancy, and read-only reasons; preserve exact strings and do not collapse them into “disk failed.”

Scope is standalone Storage Spaces. Storage cmdlets in Failover Cluster can operate at cluster level and duplicate/alter authority expectations. Storage Spaces Direct/Azure Local has a Health Service (`Get-HealthFault`, health reports, cluster nodes/volumes) and automatic repair semantics; monitor it separately. Hardware RAID and SAN/LUN providers may appear through Storage Management but are not assumed to use Storage Spaces semantics. Restrict inventory and collector deployment accordingly.

## Step 1 — Deploy a complete read-only snapshot

Store the reviewed `scriptExample` as `windows_storage_spaces_monitor/bin/Get-StorageSpacesHealth.ps1`, sign/hash/version it, and deploy only to approved standalone hosts. It calls `Get-StoragePool -IsPrimordial $false`; for each concrete pool it obtains `Get-VirtualDisk -StoragePool` and `Get-PhysicalDisk -StoragePool`. It materializes all results before output so any query failure emits `collector_error`, not a partial successful snapshot.

The script emits one manifest even when zero concrete pools exist, then one `record_type=entity` row for every pool/virtual/physical object. All rows share `snapshot_id` and `sample_epoch`. Multi-valued OperationalStatus is joined with `|` in provider order; only the exact single string `OK` normalizes to `ok`. Never default null/unknown status to Healthy/OK. Object IDs and parent pool ID establish hierarchy. Do not emit recovery passwords or unrelated file data.

Configure the supported Splunk Windows PowerShell input in local `inputs.conf`:

```ini
[powershell://StorageSpacesHealth]
script = & "$SplunkHome\etc\apps\windows_storage_spaces_monitor\bin\Get-StorageSpacesHealth.ps1"
schedule = 300
disabled = 0
index = windows
sourcetype = windows:storage_spaces:health
```

Confirm exact syntax for the installed Splunk version, inspect `splunk btool inputs list --debug`, and verify indexed `source=powershell:storage-spaces-health`. The service account needs read access to the local Storage provider, not rights to set/remove/reset/repair pools or disks. Restrict script/app ACLs and separate exception approval.

On canaries, compare every row with `Get-StoragePool -IsPrimordial $false`, `Get-VirtualDisk`, and pool-associated `Get-PhysicalDisk | Format-List *`. Validate names/IDs, multi-valued statuses, reasons, counts, hierarchy, sizes, location/model/firmware, and one manifest. A host with no configured spaces emits pool_count zero; expected inventory decides whether that is normal.

Build companion health checks for expected host with no manifest in 15 minutes; collector error; unknown schema; duplicate manifest/object; incomplete snapshot where observed rows differ from all three counts; null ID/state; nonunique object ID/type; unexpected zero pools; inventory add/remove/parent drift; future/old sample; script hash drift; and duplicate input. Alert collection/inventory owners separately.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the state search

Save as `windows_storage_spaces_degraded_entity`; schedule every 5 minutes. At 12:15, `earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m` evaluates 12:05–12:10 and leaves 5 minutes for collection. Measure lag and move both bounds together. Trigger per `host,object_type,object_id`; throttle duplicate notification for 30 minutes while preserving base rows. Recovery requires a later complete snapshot with that entity Healthy/OK and pool not read-only, or an approved inventory removal.

The base search accepts only entity rows from exact local metadata. It normalizes identity and state, then requires nonempty fields. The condition fires on non-Healthy, non-OK, or pool read-only. `reason` distinguishes health, operational, combined, and read-only branches. Because read-only is evaluated after other branches, a read-only pool also nonhealthy/non-OK receives the more severe combined reason while retaining `is_read_only` and reason fields.

`stats latest` keeps the latest state for one object in the closed window and exposes `observed_rows`; source-health proves the latest snapshot is complete. Do not expand to 24 hours, because stale degradation would persist after recovery. No CIM mirror is supplied; this is current hierarchical health, not a Change event.

## Step 3 — Validate states, completeness, and safe fault behavior

Use isolated fixtures for Healthy/OK, each health state, each operational string observed, multiple operational states joined with `|`, pool read-only alone, combined branches, null/unknown, manifest/error exclusion, duplicate rows, two snapshots, delayed events, and earliest/latest boundaries. Assert exact result columns/reasons. Validate expected-zero and unexpected-zero pool cases in companion inventory logic.

On nonproduction standalone Storage Spaces, capture a complete baseline. Use owner-approved safe methods to simulate or observe states; do not pull production disks or force failures ad hoc. A controlled disk retirement/resilience test must protect workloads/backups, name exact physical location/ID, and define expected states, repair, timeout, and abort. Confirm PowerShell, Server Manager, collector, result, alert, storage job, volume/application, and later recovery agree.

Test collector failures by denying query in a lab or using fixtures; ensure `collector_error`, not healthy zero, and no partial entity snapshot. Test script version drift, duplicate deployment, provider cache issue, host reboot, late collection, and entity count mismatch. For a planned remove/repair, ensure exception matches only exact object/change/state/time and that worsening state still pages.

Measure collector duration, entity count/bytes, Storage provider load, lag, script errors, manifest completeness, search runtime, alert delivery, and owner response. Record Windows/Storage-module/provider/forwarder/TA/Splunk versions, script hash, fixture/test/change IDs, exact UTC bounds, expected/actual state, search SID, alert/case, storage job, and recovery. Keep `draft` until owners sign off.

## Step 4 — Triage and response

For each result: (1) verify latest complete snapshot and raw Storage cmdlet state; (2) identify object and parent pool plus volume/application impact; (3) interpret exact health/operational/read-only/detached reason using Microsoft guidance; (4) inspect all sibling pool/virtual/physical entities and storage jobs; (5) correlate Windows disk/system events, controller/HBA/enclosure/cable/power/vendor telemetry and recent firmware/change; (6) verify virtual-disk resiliency/copies and remaining fault tolerance; (7) check volume/filesystem/application availability and backups; and (8) assign Windows/storage/hardware/application/telemetry owner.

Escalate critical when a pool is read-only due to Incomplete/quorum loss, virtual disk has No Redundancy/Detached, multiple disks/paths are lost, a write-critical volume/application is affected, repair fails/stalls, health worsens, or backups are unverified. Degraded redundancy can remain online but is time-sensitive before another failure.

Do not automatically set pool read-write, connect a virtual disk, reset/retire/remove a physical disk, run Repair-VirtualDisk, clear metadata, update firmware, restart storage services, or reboot. Microsoft actions depend on state/topology; incorrect changes can cause data loss. Preserve current configuration/state first and follow owner-approved storage recovery procedures. Verify recovery in a complete later snapshot plus volume/application checks and repair completion.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- **No rows/manifest:** check expected inventory, forwarder, PowerShell input, script signature/ACL, Storage module/provider, `btool`, output metadata, index, and time. Silence is not healthy.
- **`collector_error`:** run all three cmdlets under the service identity, inspect exact exception/provider cache/module, and fix query/permissions. Never convert to zero pools.
- **Unexpected zero pools:** compare owner inventory and raw cmdlets; host may be decommissioned, moved to hardware RAID/S2D, provider cache incomplete, or collector on wrong host.
- **Incomplete counts:** compare snapshot ID, manifest counts, emitted rows, script/input duplicates, output truncation, and errors. Reject snapshot for health decisions.
- **Status null/new:** inspect raw CIM object and Windows/provider version; canary schema update. Do not default to healthy.
- **Healthy plus non-OK:** operational detail intentionally fires; inspect state guidance and activity such as Removing From Pool/In Service.
- **Friendly-name collision:** route/suppress by object type and unique ID plus parent pool, never friendly name alone.
- **S2D host:** remove from this standalone deployment and use one cluster-aware Health Service authority; avoid per-node duplicate cluster snapshots.
- **Hardware RAID shows no entities:** expected if controller exposes only logical disks outside Storage Spaces. Use vendor/controller monitoring.
- **Repair ends but alert remains:** verify later complete snapshot, closed-window timing, late data, object identity, and recovery query. Do not suppress stale history manually.
grandmaExplanation: Windows can combine several drives into one protected storage pool. We check the pool, its virtual disks, and the physical drives; if any layer is unhealthy, degraded, disconnected, or read-only, we show the support team exactly which part needs attention.
hardware: Standalone Windows Server or supported Windows client systems using Microsoft Storage Spaces concrete pools. Storage Spaces Direct/Azure Local clusters require cluster-aware Health Service monitoring and a single authoritative collection design outside this UC.
